newsitem.title: TURKEY: Turkish shares dive on election fears, off lows.
newsitem.headline: Turkish shares dive on election fears, off lows.

text.p: Istanbul shares fell sharply on Thursday due to panic afternoon sales sparked by reports of early elections being discussed at junior coalition partner True Path Party's (DYP) executive board meeting, brokers said.
The IMKB National-100 which plunged 4.1 percent to an afternoon low of 1,501, recovered in late trade to close at 1,529, down 36 points, or 2.3 percent from Wednesday.
Brokers said the late recovery was due to reaction buys.
Trade volume soared to 49.42 trillion lira ($352.5 million) from Wednesday's 34.06 trillion with the help of heavy afternoon selling.
The index had surged 6.7 percent in the past three days on prospects of a new alliance to replace the Islamist-led coalition government.

"The report that polls could take place as early as October came as a shock because previous expectations were that a new coalition would be set up to rule and early polls would not take place before March 1998," said Handan Gorgun from Toros brokerage.
Private ATV television carried an unconfirmed report that early polls for October at the earliest, were discussed at the conservative DYP's executive council meeting.
The DYP executive council gave the party leader and deputy Prime Minister Tansu Ciller the authority to request early polls in bargaining with Islamist Prime Minister Necmettin Erbakan.

"We gave her the authority for early elections. An election can be held by March 1998 at the latest once the population count and ballot boxes have been prepared," the Anatolian news agency quoted DYP MP Ali Osman Sonmez as saying.

A senior DYP deputy said the ruling Islamist Welfare Party (RP) favoured handing over the premiership soon to Ciller to solve the crisis. Ciller has asked Erbakan to make her PM in a caretaker government that would take the country to the polls.

"The RP looks favourably on handing over the prime minister's job. The handover will take place soon," a member of DYP's executive council who declined to be named told Reuters. He also said elections were to be held within a year.

"Possible early polls in October may not change the current political picture. We now hope that dissidents in the DYP may act to topple the government if a new censure motion is filed," Handan Gorgun said.
A late bid to save the Islamist-led government from collapsing ran into trouble at a three-way meeting of party leaders on Wednesday.
Right-wing party leader Muhsin Yazicioglu said after the talks that he was reluctant to prop up the coalition until the alliance partners reached accord on the government's future.

Of the 254 shares traded, falls outdid rises sharply by 196 to 31 and 27 ended steady. The IMKB Industrial lost 1.97 percent to 1,445, the IMKB Services dived 4.51 percent to 1,502 and the IMKB Financial dropped 2.22 percent to 1,672.
The utility index plunged 8.23 percent and leasing-factoring index slumped 7.62 percent.

Top actives were utilities Cukurova Elektrik , up 17,500 lira at 205,000 and Aktas Elektrik , down 15,000 lira at 212,500, largely state-owned flat steel maker Eregli , up 750 lira at 17,750 and state oil refiner Tupras , up 5,000 lira 63,000. They made up 40.3 percent of the total turnover. ($ = 140180 Turkish Lire)
